chapter.heading: Ecclesiastes 4
Evil Under the Sun
chapter.v: no one to comfort them! On the side of their oppressors there was power, and there was no one to comfort them.
thought the dead who are already dead more fortunate than the living who are still alive.
better than both is he who has not yet been and has not seen the evil deeds that are done under the sun.
vanity and a striving after wind.
quietness than two hands full of toil and a striving after wind.
Again, I saw vanity under the sun:
Two are better than one, because they have a good reward for their toil.
For if they fall, one will lift up his fellow. But woe to him who is alone when he falls and has not another to lift him up!
but how can one keep warm alone?
And though a man might prevail against one who is alone, two will withstand him—a threefold cord is not quickly broken.
from prison to the throne, though in his own kingdom he had been born poor.
I saw all the living who move about under the sun, along with that youth who was to stand in the king's place.
vanity and a striving after wind.

footnotes.footnote: 4:4 The Hebrew term *hebel* can refer to a “vapor” or “mere breath”; also verses 7, 8, 16 (see note on 1:2)
